quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q2 FY2026 (02-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q2 2026 (December quarter) results: CEO Stephen Chang said revenue came in slightly above the guidance midpoint, reflecting seasonality in PCs, wearables, tablets and gaming, with AI inventory digestion further impacted by shifts in GPU allocation to prioritize data centers over graphics card markets; strength came from the tier-one U.S. smartphone customer and sequential growth in e-mobility, power tools and home appliances. CFO Yifan Liang: by product line, DMOS revenue was $101,000,000 (down 6.9% sequentially, down 10.6% year over year) and the line the transcript prints as 'ROIC' was $58,800,000 (down 19.1% sequentially, up 9.5% year over year). Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 22.2% from 24.1% last quarter and 24.2% a year ago, mainly on higher input and operation costs; non-GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.16 versus $0.13 last quarter; cash ended at $196,300,000 and average days in inventory rose to 140 days from 124 days.
quarterly_data.figure: December-quarter revenue $162,300,000 (down 6.3% year over year, down 11.1% sequentially); DMOS $101,000,000; ROIC $58,800,000; non-GAAP gross margin 22.2% (24.1% prior quarter, 24.2% a year ago); non-GAAP EPS loss $0.16; cash $196,300,000; inventory days 140 (124 prior quarter)

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q2 FY2026 (02-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Segment results for the December quarter (CEO Stephen Chang): Computing was up 5.9% year over year and down 17.1% sequentially at 49.6% of revenue, softening after an unusually strong September that benefited from tariff-related PC pull-ins and earlier AI and graphics shipments; AI and graphics customers entered a digestion phase that extended into December, further influenced by customers prioritizing production of GPUs for AI data center over traditional graphics card platforms. Consumer was down 14.9% year over year and 18.3% sequentially (11.8% of revenue), driven mainly by gaming. Communication rose 1.1% sequentially and was flat year over year (20.4% of revenue), supported by strong growth at the tier-one U.S. smartphone customer on BOM content expansion while China smartphone demand stayed uneven. Power supply and industrial was 16.7% of revenue, down 22.5% year over year and 3% sequentially, below expectations as quick charger demand came in weaker than expected.
quarterly_data.figure: Computing +5.9% YoY / -17.1% QoQ, 49.6% of revenue; Consumer -14.9% YoY / -18.3% QoQ, 11.8%; Communication +1.1% QoQ, flat YoY, 20.4%; Power supply and industrial -22.5% YoY / -3% QoQ, 16.7%

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q2 FY2026 (02-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AI data center medium-voltage MOSFET ramp (CEO Stephen Chang): AOS is shipping its high-performance medium voltage MOSFET products into infrastructure programs, including hot swap power solutions, and these are 'now moving into the build phase at leading ODMs for major hyperscale customers'; it is also expanding in AI platforms through medium voltage solutions supporting 48 volts to 12 volts intermediate bus conversion. He said AOS has 'clear visibility into demand' for the new medium voltage MOSFET (printed 'VDN voltage MOSFET' in the transcript) across a customer base that includes power supply providers, module makers, cloud service providers and major hyperscalers, and that the medium-voltage business was already contributing to December results and would be more visible in the March quarter.

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q2 FY2026 (02-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AI GPU VRM opportunity below plan, AI share of computing (CEO Stephen Chang): the AI opportunity 'is somewhat less than our original expectations regarding selling solutions to power GPUs directly at the VRM stage', but it is expanding beyond total solutions for VRMs into medium voltage MOSFETs used earlier in the power conversion chain, which already showed in the quarter's results. AI and graphics-related revenue ranged roughly 20% to 25% of computing in some calendar 2025 quarters; he said he could not give a hard number but 'can see that portion growing to 50% of computing, and it could be higher depending on how quickly we penetrate opportunities', with medium voltage expected to generate quicker returns even this calendar year.
quarterly_data.figure: AI and graphics roughly 20% to 25% of computing in some calendar 2025 quarters; CEO sees it growing to 50% of computing (no hard number)

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q2 FY2026 (02-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Roadmap and R&D (CEO Stephen Chang, CFO Yifan Liang): AOS is 'preparing for 800-volt solutions and wide band gap solutions for higher-voltage applications' and developing other IC sockets, alongside medium voltage 48V to 12V power conversion that reaches ecosystem partners and cloud service providers beyond specific AI platforms. R&D is being increased in three core areas (AI, PC total solutions and smartphone high-performance battery protection); the CFO said this is about a 25% increase in R&D expense for calendar 2026 versus the prior year, ramping gradually through the June and September quarters. The CEO said calendar 2026 should show tangible results, with 'more meaningful acceleration in 2027 and beyond as new platforms and programs ramp'.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D expense up about 25% in calendar 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q2 FY2026 (02-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: March-quarter guidance (CFO Yifan Liang): revenue approximately $160,000,000 plus or minus $10,000,000; GAAP gross margin 20.2% plus or minus 1% and non-GAAP gross margin 21% plus or minus 1% (lower on reduced utilization around Lunar New Year, expected to rebound in June toward the December 2025 or September 2025 levels); GAAP operating expenses $52,000,000 and non-GAAP $45,000,000, each plus or minus $1,000,000, the increase mostly R&D. By segment (CEO): computing down low single digits sequentially as PC softness is mostly offset by AI data center, graphics cards and tablets; consumer up mid-single digits on a gaming recovery; communication down mid-single digits on tier-one U.S. smartphone seasonality; power supply up mid-single digits on quick chargers and DC fans. The CEO expects March 'to mark a near-term low point for revenue and margin', with growth returning beginning in June; calendar 2026 'may reflect modest growth' with stronger growth into 2027 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: March-quarter revenue approximately $160,000,000 plus or minus $10,000,000; GAAP gross margin 20.2% +/- 1%; non-GAAP gross margin 21% +/- 1%; GAAP opex $52,000,000, non-GAAP opex $45,000,000 (+/- $1,000,000)

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q2 FY2026 (02-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Midterm target model and pricing (CFO Yifan Liang): the midterm target model is $1,000,000,000 in revenue, 30% non-GAAP gross margin and 20% operating margin; reaching 30% gross margin depends on new products, better product mix and a normal pricing environment. quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q2 FY2026 (02-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: PC and smartphone content (CEO Stephen Chang): overall PC unit demand in calendar 2026 is expected to be constrained by tightening memory supply, and visibility into the PC market is limited by memory shortages, but increased BOM content from AOS total solutions (controller paired with driver MOSFETs) on new platforms such as Intel's 'Camberlake' (as printed) is expected to offset it. In smartphones, investments in silicon and packaging for battery protection plus the move to higher charging currents secured increased BOM content with top-tier customers, and AOS sustains high share in premium phones; further growth is expected in calendar 2026 as new models launch with higher charging currents.
